papers.title: From RNA design to delivery: Computational strategies for functional RNA therapeutics.
papers.abstract: RNA therapeutics provide a revolutionary means of treating a variety of diseases by precisely regulating gene expression and protein synthesis, with great medical significance. However, there are three key challenges to its clinical application: the inherent instability of RNA, the need for controlled regulation of RNA function, and the lack of an efficient delivery system. Computational strategies provide complementary tools for analyzing and optimizing RNA sequence, structure, function, and delivery, accelerating the rational design of RNAs and the optimization of delivery systems. This revi
papers.summary: This review surveys computational strategies that support the development of RNA therapeutics, covering RNA sequence/structure/function design as well as optimization of delivery systems. It frames the field around three clinical challenges—RNA instability, need for controlled regulation, and inefficient delivery—and discusses how computational tools can accelerate rational design.

papers.title: Luteolin alleviates myocardial fibrosis through the ERK1/2-GATA4 pathway by inhibiting oxidative stress and EndMT.
papers.abstract: Myocardial fibrosis is a common pathological feature of cardiovascular diseases and is closely associated with oxidative stress, apoptosis, extracellular matrix remodeling, and endothelial-to-mesenchymal transition (EndMT). Luteolin (Lut), a naturally occurring flavonoid, exhibits cardioprotective properties; however, its anti-fibrotic effects and underlying mechanisms remain unclear.
papers.summary: This study investigates whether luteolin, a natural flavonoid, can reduce myocardial fibrosis and proposes that it acts by inhibiting oxidative stress and endothelial-to-mesenchymal transition (EndMT) via the ERK1/2-GATA4 signaling pathway. The findings suggest a mechanistic basis for luteolin's cardioprotective effects, though the abstract only outlines the study's aims rather than reporting specific results.

papers.title: Acrylamide-associated gastric cancer progression involves RRM2-related nucleotide metabolic dysregulation and immune evasion.
papers.abstract: Acrylamide (AA) is a widespread environmental contaminant and a probable human carcinogen. Its role in gastric cancer (GC), however, remains unclear. We investigated whether AA-associated molecular changes may contribute to GC through altered nucleotide metabolism. Integration of CTD, MSigDB, and GeneCards identified 11 AA-nucleotide metabolism-GC-related genes (ANGRGs). Binding-pocket analysis and non-covalent molecular docking prioritized RRM2 as a candidate associated with AA-related molecular effects. These in silico analyses did not model covalent adduct formation. RRM2 was overexpressed
papers.summary: This study integrates multiple databases to identify genes linking acrylamide exposure, nucleotide metabolism, and gastric cancer, prioritizing RRM2 as a key candidate through molecular docking. The findings suggest that acrylamide-associated molecular changes may drive gastric cancer progression via RRM2-related nucleotide metabolic dysregulation and immune evasion, though the in silico analyses did not model covalent adduct formation.

papers.title: Elucidating the beneficial effects of gut microbiota-derived metabolites in treating hepatocellular carcinoma: an integrated network pharmacology, molecular docking, and single-cell sequencing analysis.
papers.abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is the most common type of liver cancer and the third leading cause of cancer-related mortality worldwide. While accumulating evidence has highlighted the beneficial effects of gut microbiota (GM)-derived metabolites in HCC treatment, the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. We retrieved GM-derived metabolites from gutMGene v2.0, acquired their targets using the Similarity Ensemble Approach (SEA) and Swiss Target Prediction (STP), and identified HCC-related targets from public databases. Overlapping targets were then obtained via Venn diagram analysis. We constr
papers.summary: This study integrates network pharmacology, molecular docking, and single-cell sequencing to investigate how gut microbiota-derived metabolites may help treat hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). The authors identified shared targets between microbiota metabolites and HCC-related genes, then used docking and single-cell data to propose mechanistic pathways underlying these beneficial effects.

papers.title: Bridging the accuracy-speed divide in reactive molecular dynamics with QuantaMind MD.
papers.abstract: Simulating chemical reactivity remains a central challenge in molecular dynamics, historically constrained by the trade-off between ab initio accuracy and classical efficiency. We present QuantaMind, a machine learning force field (MLFF) framework that attains density functional theory (DFT)-level accuracy, enabling fully reactive simulations of complex molecular systems. QuantaMind achieves exceptional numerical stability over tens-of-nanosecond trajectories, maintaining accuracy throughout long-time reactive dynamics. It reproduces spontaneous bond formation and cleavage in key chemical proc
papers.summary: QuantaMind is a machine learning force field that achieves density functional theory-level accuracy while remaining efficient enough for long reactive molecular dynamics simulations. It maintains numerical stability over tens-of-nanosecond trajectories and correctly reproduces spontaneous bond formation and cleavage, bridging the traditional accuracy-speed trade-off.

papers.title: Docking-score landscapes shape active-learning performance across Vina, Glide, and SILCS.
papers.abstract: The rapid expansion of large chemical libraries has created a need for virtual screening workflows that are both efficient and accurate. Active learning (AL) offers a scalable strategy by iteratively training surrogate models to prioritize promising compounds and reduce the number of required docking calculations. However, direct benchmarking of active-learning protocols across docking engines remains limited. In this study, we ask whether docking scores generated by different docking engines affect AL performance and what factors underlie these differences. To do so, we compare four active-le
papers.summary: This study benchmarks active-learning workflows across three docking engines (Vina, Glide, SILCS) and finds that the shape of the docking-score landscape strongly influences how well active learning performs. Differences in score distributions and smoothness across engines lead to varying efficiency in prioritizing promising compounds, suggesting that AL protocols should be tuned to the specific docking engine used.

papers.title: Multiscale investigation of CO2 capture in 1,2,4-triazolium-based ionic liquids and porous copolymers using density functional theory and molecular dynamics.
papers.abstract: Capturing carbon dioxide (CO2) directly from the atmosphere has become an essential approach in efforts to address climate change, particularly within broader carbon capture and storage frameworks. Among the materials explored for direct air capture, ionic liquids (ILs) stand out as their chemical structure can be finely adjusted to optimise how they interact with CO2, including both capture and subsequent transformation. Building on this concept, poly(ionic liquid)s (PILs) have been developed as an advanced class of materials that provide greater structural stability and enhanced interaction
papers.summary: This study uses density functional theory and molecular dynamics simulations to investigate how 1,2,4-triazolium-based ionic liquids and their derived porous copolymers (poly(ionic liquid)s) capture CO2. The multiscale modeling approach aims to clarify the molecular-level interactions that govern CO2 uptake, supporting the rational design of tunable materials for direct air capture.

papers.title: Structural Overview of GLP-1 Analogs.
papers.abstract: Glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) analogs exert potent metabolic effects through structural features that govern receptor engagement, signaling, and pharmacokinetics. Key structural determinants include N-terminal modifications that confer resistance to dipeptidyl peptidase-4 degradation, as well as C-terminal and backbone elements that stabilize peptide helicity and enhance GLP-1 receptor affinity. Lipidation and albumin-binding strategies prolong systemic exposure by increasing circulating half-life, forming the basis of long-acting agents such as liraglutide and semaglutide. Structural variat
papers.summary: This review examines how the structural features of GLP-1 analogs—such as N-terminal modifications, C-terminal and backbone elements, and lipidation/albumin-binding strategies—determine their resistance to degradation, receptor affinity, and circulating half-life. These structural insights explain the design of long-acting agents like liraglutide and semaglutide. The paper provides a consolidated structural overview relevant to therapeutic development of GLP-1-based drugs.

papers.title: Ultrasound-assisted extraction of polyphenols from Moutan Cortex using natural deep eutectic solvent: Optimization, molecular mechanisms, and lipid-lowering activity.
papers.abstract: Moutan Cortex is a valuable medicinal resource rich in bioactive polyphenols, yet its sustainable valorization is often hindered by the inefficiencies and environmental concerns associated with conventional extraction methods. In this study, a green and efficient ultrasound-assisted extraction (UAE) strategy was developed using a betaine-levulinic acid (Bet-LevA) natural deep eutectic solvent (NADES). An intelligent optimization approach was applied to determine the optimal extraction conditions, achieving a maximum total polyphenol content of 27.03 ± 0.41 mg GAE/g DW, which was 1.93-fold high
papers.summary: This study develops an ultrasound-assisted extraction method using a natural deep eutectic solvent (betaine-levulinic acid) to recover polyphenols from Moutan Cortex, achieving nearly double the yield of conventional methods. The authors optimize conditions via an intelligent approach, explore the molecular mechanisms, and demonstrate lipid-lowering activity of the extracted polyphenols.

papers.title: Dissecting affinity determinants of benzotriazine-based ligands at sigma-1 receptor: a multilevel molecular dynamics analysis.
papers.abstract: The sigma-1 receptor (S1R) is a chaperone protein involved in several physiological and pathological processes and represents an attractive target for the development of neuroactive and anticancer agents. Among S1R ligands, 3,3-disubstituted 3,4-dihydro-1,2,4-benzotriazines constitute a pharmacologically relevant but mechanistically underexplored scaffold. In this work, we computationally re-examine a representative set of benzotriazine derivatives previously synthesized and pharmacologically characterized by Fabio Sparatore and coworkers, integrating their published experimental binding affin
papers.summary: This study uses multilevel molecular dynamics simulations to dissect the structural and energetic determinants of binding affinity for benzotriazine-based ligands at the sigma-1 receptor. By computationally re-examining a set of previously synthesized and pharmacologically characterized derivatives, the authors identify key interactions governing ligand recognition at S1R. The work provides mechanistic insight into an underexplored scaffold relevant to neuroactive and anticancer drug development.

papers.title: Engineered Transformer Base Editor with Enhanced Editing Efficiency.
papers.abstract: Canonical cytosine base editors (CBEs) achieve precise C-to-T conversions without inducing DNA double-strand breaks (DSBs), yet their clinical potential remains hampered by substantial off-target (OT) mutations. The recently developed transformer base editor (tBE) significantly reduces both genomic and transcriptomic OT mutations by using a cleavable deoxycytidine deaminase inhibitor (dCDI) domain. However, the modest base editing efficiency limits its broader applications. Here, through rational deaminase engineering and fusion of a uracil DNA glycosylase inhibitor (UGI) domain, we developed
papers.summary: The authors engineered an improved transformer base editor (tBE) by rationally modifying the deaminase and adding a uracil DNA glycosylase inhibitor (UGI) domain, aiming to boost editing efficiency while preserving the low off-target profile of the original tBE. This addresses a key limitation of tBE—its modest base editing efficiency—which has restricted its broader application, especially for clinical genome editing.

papers.title: Pharmacological modulation of GPR84 revealed by dual states structures and immune functional assays.
papers.abstract: G-protein-coupled receptor 84 (GPR84) is an orphan class A GPCR selectively activated by medium chain fatty acids and highly expressed in immune cells, where it modulates pro-inflammatory signaling. The structural basis of GPR84 inactivation and antagonism has remained unclear, limiting the rational design of pathway-selective modulators despite its clinical relevance in metabolic inflammation and fibrotic diseases. Here, we report cryo-electron microscopy structures of human GPR84 in inactive and active states. The 3.5 Å inactive structure bound to the antagonist GLPG1205 reveals a lid-like c
papers.summary: This study presents cryo-electron microscopy structures of the orphan GPCR GPR84 in both inactive (antagonist-bound) and active states, revealing the structural basis for its inactivation and antagonism. Combined with immune functional assays, the work clarifies how pharmacological modulation of GPR84 occurs, aiding rational design of pathway-selective modulators for inflammatory and fibrotic diseases.

papers.title: Biological Investigation of Novel Pyrazole-Based Anticancer Scaffolds: A Trinity of Synthetic Methodologies on Computational Assessment of IC50 Against Human Cancer Cell Lines MCF-7, MDA-MB and HeLa.
papers.abstract: Aurora kinase A (AURKA) is a key regulator of mitotic progression and is frequently overexpressed in human malignancies, making it an attractive therapeutic target for the development of targeted anticancer agents. The present study aimed to design and synthesize sixteen novel pyrazole derivatives (Pz-01 to Pz-16) as potential AURKA-targeted anticancer agents and to evaluate their anticancer activity, AURKA-binding potential, and SAR using integrated experimental and computational approaches. The synthesized compounds were screened for cytotoxic activity against human breast cancer (MCF-7 and
papers.journal: European journal of pharmaceutical sciences : official journal of the European Federation for Pharmaceutical Sciences
papers.summary: This study designed and synthesized sixteen novel pyrazole derivatives as potential AURKA-targeted anticancer agents, evaluating their cytotoxicity against breast cancer (MCF-7, MDA-MB) and cervical cancer (HeLa) cell lines. Computational docking and SAR analyses were integrated with experimental IC50 measurements to assess AURKA binding and anticancer potential. The work identifies pyrazole scaffolds as promising leads for further anticancer drug development.

papers.title: Domain-Swapped LuxR-Type Quorum Sensing Receptors Reveal Divergent Ligand-Response Mechanisms among Homologues.
papers.abstract: LuxI/R quorum sensing controls diverse cell density-dependent behaviors in gram-negative bacteria, yet the molecular basis of LuxR-type receptor response to ligands remains poorly defined. This gap limits both mechanistic understanding of signaling and the rational design of synthetic LuxR modulators. LuxR homologues exhibit two response modes: associative receptors require N-acyl l-homoserine lactone (AHL) signal binding to enable DNA binding and transcriptional activation, whereas dissociative receptors are active without ligand and inhibited upon AHL binding. Herein, we dissect determinants
papers.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
papers.summary: This study investigates how LuxR-type quorum sensing receptors respond to ligands, focusing on the structural basis for two distinct response modes: associative receptors that require AHL binding to activate transcription, and dissociative receptors that are active without ligand and inhibited by AHL. By analyzing domain-swapped receptors, the authors reveal divergent ligand-response mechanisms among homologues, providing insights that could aid in designing synthetic LuxR modulators.

papers.title: Organotin-Catalyzed Synthesis, Characterization, Anticancer and Antioxidant Activities, and Molecular Modeling Studies of Nimesulide Ureas as Potential MetAP (Type II) Inhibitors.
papers.abstract: In this study, a new series of nimesulide-derived ureas (3a-j) was designed and synthesized to investigate structural modifications of nimesulide and to evaluate their biological activity. The compounds were obtained in high yields (68-88%) under organotin-catalyzed conditions, and their structures were unequivocally established using comprehensive spectroscopic techniques, including 1H NMR, 13C NMR, FTIR, and HRMS. Following structural confirmation, the antioxidant properties of the synthesized derivatives were evaluated using the 2,2-diphenyl-1-picrylhydrazyl (DPPH) radical scavenging assay,
papers.summary: This study synthesized a new series of nimesulide-derived urea compounds using organotin catalysis and characterized them spectroscopically. The compounds were tested for antioxidant activity via DPPH assays and evaluated as potential anticancer agents targeting MetAP type II enzymes, with molecular modeling supporting the binding predictions.

papers.title: Molecular Simulation Study of Crude Oil Desorption Behavior during Low-Salinity Waterflooding.
papers.abstract: To address the unresolved mechanisms and debated microscale interactions governing crude oil desorption during low-salinity waterflooding in tight oil reservoirs, this study focuses on molecular-level interactions within the waterflooding process. Using molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, we constructed a multicomponent crude oil model comprising n-dodecane, toluene, and pyridine, along with waterflooding systems at two salinities (5000 ppm and 50,000 ppm). The microscale desorption behavior of individual crude oil components from a hydroxylated quartz surface during low-salinity waterfloodin
papers.summary: This study uses molecular dynamics simulations to investigate how crude oil components (n-dodecane, toluene, pyridine) desorb from hydroxylated quartz surfaces during low-salinity waterflooding at two salinity levels. It aims to clarify debated microscale mechanisms governing oil recovery in tight reservoirs by examining molecular-level interactions between oil, water, and rock.

papers.title: Prodrug-like Quinone Containing Two Redox-Active Centers Induces Ferroptosis in Prostate Cancer Cells with Cytotoxic Action Partially Depending on NAD(P)H Quinone Dehydrogenase 1 (NQO1).
papers.abstract: Naphthoquinones are redox-active compounds with antitumor potential, often linked to NQO1 overexpression in cancer cells. This study evaluated the cytotoxic activity of two synthetic 1,4-naphthoquinones, compound 1 and its dual redox analog, compound 4, against NQO1-overexpressing DU-145 prostate cancer cells through integrated in vitro, enzymatic, and computational (docking and quantum) analyses. Compound 4 exhibited over 2-fold greater cytotoxicity against DU-145 cells compared to nontumor MRC-5 cells, while maintaining low hemolytic activity. Evidence of membrane damage, ROS generation, lip
papers.summary: This study synthesized two 1,4-naphthoquinone compounds and tested their anticancer activity against NQO1-overexpressing DU-145 prostate cancer cells. The dual redox-active compound 4 showed over 2-fold greater cytotoxicity toward cancer cells than normal cells and induced ferroptosis via ROS generation and membrane damage, with its cytotoxic action partially dependent on the NQO1 enzyme. These findings suggest that prodrug-like quinones targeting NQO1 could be a promising strategy for prostate cancer therapy.

papers.title: Combined multi-parameter filtering and prioritization of a chemical library for cancer disease target.
papers.abstract: Cancer is a multifactorial disease and remains a significant problem owing to its complex nature. There is an urgent need to identify and design hybrid anticancer drugs that achieve a desired biological effect by combining two or more pharmacophores into a single molecule. Herein, we utilized MOLHYBRID program to generate a chemical library of 46740 unique molecules based on known anticancer pharmacophores and targeting the cancer protein, using the crystal structure of the B-Raf V600E oncogenic mutant in complex PLX4033 (vemurafenib) (PDB ID: 3OG7). The B-Raf V600E mutant is prevalent cancer-
papers.summary: The authors used the MOLHYBRID program to generate a library of 46,740 hybrid molecules combining known anticancer pharmacophores, targeting the B-Raf V600E oncogenic mutant based on its crystal structure with vemurafenib. They then applied multi-parameter filtering and prioritization to narrow down candidate compounds for further development as hybrid anticancer drugs.

papers.title: Rational Design of Au@co-MOF Synergistic Platform for Ultrasensitive Monitoring of Dopamine in Human Biological Fluids.
papers.abstract: This study presents the rational design and application of engineered metal-organic framework (MOF) hybrids, tailored to exhibit accelerated electron transfer kinetics and enhanced molecular recognition capabilities for the high-sensitivity detection of dopamine (DA). Specifically, an enzyme-free electrochemical sensing platform was constructed using Au@Co-MOF nanocomposites, which were synthesized via a controllable in situ growth approach. Au nanoparticles (AuNPs) were uniformly anchored onto the [Co3(TMA)3(H2O)5]n (where TMA = 1,3,5-trimesic acid) framework containing coordinatively unsatur
papers.summary: This study reports an enzyme-free electrochemical sensor for dopamine detection built from gold nanoparticles grown in situ on a cobalt-based metal-organic framework (Au@Co-MOF). The hybrid platform shows accelerated electron transfer and enhanced molecular recognition, enabling ultrasensitive dopamine quantification in human biological fluids.

papers.title: In Silico Identification of Novel Leads as Potential DPP-IV Inhibitors as Antidiabetic Agents Using Virtual Screening.
papers.abstract: Purpose: Dipeptidyl peptidase-IV (DPP-IV) is a validated therapeutic target for type 2 diabetes mellitus due to its role in incretin hormone degradation. This study aimed to identify novel small-molecule DPP-IV inhibitors from the ECBD database using an integrated virtual screening and molecular dynamics (MD) approach, acknowledging that experimental validation is necessary to confirm biological activity. Methods: Structure-based virtual screening of 5,500 ECBD compounds was performed using molecular docking to identify high-affinity ligands, followed by interaction analysis with key catalytic
papers.summary: This study used molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations to screen 5,500 compounds from the ECBD database against DPP-IV, a validated target for type 2 diabetes, aiming to identify novel small-molecule inhibitors. The authors report high-affinity candidate leads based on binding interactions with key catalytic residues, though experimental validation is still needed to confirm biological activity.

papers.title: Cross-docking and redocking reveal distinct determinants of success in physics-based and AI-driven binding pose prediction in protein-ligand complexes.
papers.abstract: Protein-ligand pose prediction is central to structure-based drug discovery, yet the relative performance of physics-based and AI-driven methods under realistic cross-docking conditions remains insufficiently characterized. Here, we compare physics-based docking methods (AutoDock4, AutoDock Vina, and DOCK 6) with data-driven approaches, including the deep-learning model GNINA 1.3 and the diffusion-based frameworks AlphaFold 3, Boltz-2, and DiffDock. Performance was evaluated using standardised redocking and cross-docking protocols across three Alzheimer's disease targets representing distinct
papers.summary: This study benchmarks physics-based docking tools (AutoDock4, AutoDock Vina, DOCK 6) against AI-driven pose predictors (GNINA 1.3, AlphaFold 3, Boltz-2, DiffDock) on three Alzheimer's disease targets under both redocking and cross-docking conditions. The results show that the two method classes succeed for different reasons, with AI methods excelling in some realistic cross-docking scenarios while physics-based tools retain advantages elsewhere. The work highlights that pose prediction success depends on distinct determinants for each approach, informing how these tools should be chosen and combined in structure-based drug discovery.

papers.title: Structure-based design of soluble prefusion-stabilized herpes simplex virus type 2 glycoprotein B antigens.
papers.abstract: Herpes simplex virus type 2 (HSV-2) infection causes recurrent genital herpes throughout life, yet no vaccines have been approved. Glycoprotein B (gB) is a class III fusion protein that mediates HSV-2 entry by transitioning from a metastable prefusion conformation to a stable postfusion conformation. Here, using structure-based design, we stabilize HSV-2 gB in its prefusion conformation. A 2.8 Å resolution cryo-EM structure reveals a closed state of prefusion gB, which differs from recently published open states. Vaccination of mice with protein subunit and mRNA-based vaccines of pre- and post
papers.summary: This study uses structure-based design to engineer soluble HSV-2 glycoprotein B (gB) antigens locked in the prefusion conformation, which is the key target for neutralizing antibodies. A 2.8 Å cryo-EM structure reveals a closed prefusion state distinct from previously reported open states, and vaccination of mice with protein and mRNA versions of these stabilized antigens shows promise for HSV-2 vaccine development.

papers.title: Enhanced Line Search Improves Robustness and Efficiency of Pose Sampling in Protein-Ligand Docking.
papers.abstract: Physics-based protein-ligand docking critically depends on efficient pose sampling, yet established sampling and local refinement algorithms can be inefficient and unstable in the highly nonconvex energy landscapes characteristic of protein-ligand interactions. To address this limitation, we introduce an enhanced local optimization strategy based on curved line search (CLS) and integrate it into AutoDock Vina, resulting in Vina_CLS. The proposed method enables more flexible step-size selection during local refinement and improves convergence in challenging regions of the energy landscape. Acro
papers.journal: Journal of chemical theory and computation
papers.summary: The authors introduce an enhanced line search method called curved line search (CLS) and integrate it into AutoDock Vina to create Vina_CLS, improving pose sampling in protein-ligand docking. This approach enables more flexible step-size selection during local refinement, leading to better convergence in challenging regions of the energy landscape. The method aims to improve both robustness and efficiency of docking pose sampling.

papers.title: Enhancing prediction accuracy for enzyme activity engineering through sequence co-evolution and epistatic relationship modeling.
papers.abstract: Conventional enzyme engineering strategies, such as directed evolution with structure-based analysis, are limited by laborious workflows and by the need to screen extensive enzyme libraries. Computational models based on multiple sequence alignment, such as SCANEER, have streamlined these engineering strategies, enabling the successful prediction of single-site mutations that enhance enzyme activity. However, when combining predicted mutations to improve enzyme performance or expand mutational space, such approaches often fail due to epistatic interactions among amino acid residues, which can
papers.summary: This paper presents a computational method that improves prediction of enzyme activity-enhancing mutations by incorporating sequence co-evolution and epistatic relationships, addressing the failure of existing tools like SCANEER when combining single-site mutations. The approach enables more reliable engineering of enzymes with multiple mutations, reducing the need for laborious directed evolution and large-scale screening.

papers.title: ProRB: a structure-free unified framework for joint prediction and design of protein-RNA interactions.
papers.abstract: While protein-RNA interactions are fundamental to post-transcriptional processes, achieving a holistic understanding of their regulatory logic remains challenging. Current computational models often treat binding affinity, interface mapping, and RNA design as isolated tasks, thereby failing to provide a unified perspective of the protein-RNA interactome. Here, we introduce ProRB, a unified sequence-based framework that jointly estimates protein-RNA binding affinity, predicts binding interfaces in proteins and RNAs, and generates protein-binding RNA sequences from protein sequences. By fusing p
papers.summary: ProRB is a sequence-based deep learning framework that unifies three protein-RNA interaction tasks: predicting binding affinity, mapping binding interfaces on both proteins and RNAs, and designing protein-binding RNA sequences. Unlike prior models that handle these tasks in isolation, ProRB provides a single structure-free model for holistic analysis of the protein-RNA interactome.

papers.title: Efficacy of icariin in polycystic ovary syndrome: Cathepsin S as a key target revealed by computational and experimental evidence.
papers.abstract: Polycystic Ovary Syndrome (PCOS) is a prevalent female reproductive and endocrine disorder. Effective and safe therapeutic strategies remain to be further explored. This study aimed to investigate the mechanisms of icariin (ICA) in PCOS. By executing weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA) across seven Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) datasets and cross-referencing with ICA targets from five pharmacological databases, we identified 96 potential genes. An optimized machine learning framework evaluating 113 algorithm combinations and summary data-based Mendelian randomization (SMR) ref
papers.summary: This study combined network analysis of seven GEO datasets with pharmacological databases to identify 96 candidate genes linking icariin to polycystic ovary syndrome, then used a machine learning framework and Mendelian randomization to prioritize cathepsin S as a key target. Experimental validation supported icariin's efficacy against PCOS via this target. The work illustrates an integrative computational-experimental pipeline for drug repurposing in a common endocrine disorder.

papers.title: Characterizing CCR2 homodimers using homology-derived and AI-predicted interfaces.
papers.abstract: Deciphering the functional roles of G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs) oligomers requires defining their structural organization, which remains a challenge due to the inherent flexibility of their 7 transmembrane (TM) domains. Here, we focused on determining homodimer interfaces of the chemokine receptor CCR2, a major component of the inflammatory response, for which no antagonist has yet been approved. We generated models of CCR2 homodimers combining homology modeling, a conventional in silico approach, or an AI-based AlphaFold-Multimer predictions, with molecular dynamics simulations. We de
papers.summary: This study models the homodimer interfaces of the chemokine receptor CCR2 by combining traditional homology modeling and AI-based AlphaFold-Multimer predictions with molecular dynamics simulations. The work aims to clarify how CCR2 self-associates structurally, which could inform future drug design targeting this inflammatory receptor.

papers.title: Antimicrobial peptides as computational candidates for SARS-CoV-2 papain-like protease inhibition.
papers.abstract: SARS-CoV-2 papain-like protease (PLpro) remains an attractive antiviral target because of its dual role in viral polyprotein processing and host immune modulation. In this study, we employed an exploratory structure-based computational workflow to identify antimicrobial peptide scaffolds with predicted PLpro-binding potential. A total of 6,615 peptides compiled from public databases were screened using protein-peptide docking, followed by molecular dynamics simulations and end-state binding energy analysis for selected complexes. Among the prioritized candidates, peptides 33,035 and 17,047 sho
papers.summary: This study used a computational workflow combining protein-peptide docking, molecular dynamics simulations, and binding energy analysis to screen 6,615 antimicrobial peptides from public databases for potential binding to the SARS-CoV-2 papain-like protease (PLpro). Two peptides (33,035 and 17,047) emerged as prioritized candidates with predicted PLpro-binding potential, suggesting antimicrobial peptides as possible scaffolds for antiviral development.

papers.title: Structural determinants of Mac1 inhibition: Lessons from ligand binding patterns.
papers.abstract: This study comprehensively analyzes how various inhibitors bind to the SARS-CoV-2 macrodomain Mac1, a key protein implicated in hampering the host's immune response following viral infection. In this study we used volume-based metadynamics simulations to investigate the binding mechanisms of ADP-ribose and two Mac1 inhibitors: the adenine-analogue GS-441524 and the non-adenine-analogue S09. By combining free-energy simulations with a bioinformatic analysis, we aimed at determining whether the binding patterns observed for the selected ligands can be generalized across Mac1 inhibitors and can b
papers.summary: This study uses volume-based metadynamics simulations to dissect how three ligands—ADP-ribose, GS-441524, and S09—bind to the SARS-CoV-2 macrodomain Mac1, a protein that helps the virus evade host immunity. By combining free-energy calculations with bioinformatic analysis, the authors assess whether binding patterns are generalizable across different Mac1 inhibitors. The work provides structural insights that could guide the design of improved Mac1-targeting antiviral drugs.

papers.title: DyProL: Dynamic Ensemble Representation Learning for Protein-Nucleic Acid Binding Site Prediction.
papers.abstract: Protein-nucleic acid interactions play central roles in gene regulation and cellular function, and extensive efforts have been devoted to predicting nucleic acid binding sites from protein structures. However, protein-nucleic acid recognition is inherently dynamic, whereas most existing computational approaches rely on single static conformations, limiting their ability to capture conformational heterogeneity underlying binding. Here, we present DyProL, an ensemble-based conformational representation learning framework that models proteins as ensembles of conformations sampled from equilibrium
papers.summary: DyProL is a computational framework that predicts protein-nucleic acid binding sites by modeling proteins as ensembles of dynamic conformations rather than single static structures. By learning representations from conformational ensembles sampled from equilibrium, it captures the structural heterogeneity that underlies binding recognition. This ensemble-based approach aims to improve prediction accuracy over methods relying on static conformations.

papers.title: A Predictive Strength Model for Cu/Ni Nanolayered Composites with FCC Interfacial Layers Under Loading Parallel to the Interface.
papers.abstract: Nanolayered metallic composites exhibit ultra-high strength but suffer from inadequate ductility. Constructing interfacial layers becomes an effective strategy to enhance their strength and ductility. However, extensive experimental studies have focused on the strengthening and toughening mechanism of some special interfacial layers under loading normal to the interface, a systematic understanding of how interfacial layer characteristics influence the mechanical response remains unclear, especially under loading parallel to the interfaces. Here, molecular dynamics simulations using the LAMMPS
papers.summary: This paper uses molecular dynamics simulations to build a predictive strength model for Cu/Ni nanolayered composites that contain face-centered-cubic (FCC) interfacial layers, focusing on loading applied parallel to the interfaces. It systematically examines how interfacial layer characteristics influence mechanical response, addressing a gap left by prior work that mostly studied loading normal to the interface.

papers.title: Engineering the Stability of Sucrose Synthase to Enable Efficient Coupled Production of UDP-Glucuronic Acid.
papers.abstract: The biocatalytic synthesis of UDP-glucuronic acid (UDPGA), a key precursor for glucuronides and high-value carbohydrates, is limited by an unstable UDP-glucose (UDPG) supply in coupled systems. In this study, through an extensive screening of 10 sucrose synthases derived from both eukaryotic and prokaryotic microorganisms, we identified a broad-spectrum, highly efficient enzymatic scaffold suitable for the synthesis of UDP-sugars. A rational design integrating PROSS and ThermoMPNN algorithms with molecular dynamics (MD) analysis yielded the V353L mutant, which retained 97% of wild-type activit
papers.summary: The study screened 10 sucrose synthases to find a stable, efficient enzyme for producing UDP-glucuronic acid (UDPGA), a valuable precursor for glucuronides and carbohydrates. Using computational design (PROSS, ThermoMPNN, and molecular dynamics), they engineered a V353L mutant that retained 97% of wild-type activity while improving stability, enabling more efficient coupled production of UDPGA.

papers.title: Preparation, Structural Features, Bioactivities, and Food Application of Oyster Mushroom Polysaccharides: A Review.
papers.abstract: Water-soluble oyster mushroom polysaccharides (OMPs) are multifunctional biopolymers with growing relevance in food and health-related applications. This review summarizes recent progress in the extraction, purification, structural features, biological activities, and food applications of OMPs, with particular emphasis on tentative structure-activity relationships constrained by heterogeneous experimental evidence. Conventional and emerging extraction approaches, including hot water, enzyme-assisted, ultrasound-assisted, and microwave-assisted methods, are compared in terms of yield and struct
papers.summary: This review compiles recent research on water-soluble polysaccharides from oyster mushrooms, covering extraction and purification methods, structural characteristics, biological activities, and food applications. It highlights tentative structure-activity relationships while noting that heterogeneous experimental evidence limits firm conclusions.

papers.title: Recent Exploration of Right-Handed D-Sulfonyl-γ-AApeptides as Potential Tools Toward α-Helical Mimicry.
papers.abstract: Over the last 15 years, our laboratory has explored peptidomimetics in diverse research areas, including AApeptide folding, structure-based design, combinatorial screening, and supramolecular chemistry. Through these efforts, we successfully introduced a new subclass of AApeptides known as sulfonyl-γ-AApeptides. In recent years, we took advantage of the synthetic scaffold and rationally designed and developed helices targeting a series of protein-protein interactions. This Perspective summarizes our recent advances in developing right-handed helical D-sulfonyl-γ-AApeptides, which closely resem
papers.summary: This perspective reviews the laboratory's development of sulfonyl-γ-AApeptides, a class of peptidomimetics designed to mimic α-helical structures. The authors highlight how right-handed helical D-sulfonyl-γ-AApeptides can be rationally designed to target protein-protein interactions, offering potential as therapeutic tools.

papers.title: Standardizing pre-existing anti-PEG antibody detection: A key to clarifying their binding features and clinical relevance.
papers.abstract: Polyethylene glycol (PEG) is a widely used pharmaceutical excipient to improve drug solubility and prolong in vivo circulation duration. Although it was initially considered non-immunogenic, recent studies have confirmed the ubiquitous presence of anti-PEG antibodies pre-existing in human, influencing the efficacy and safety of multiple PEGylated medicines. Due to the contradictions of current anti-PEG antibody detection methods and unclear induction mechanism of human pre-existing anti-PEG antibodies, the actual prevalence, binding features, and biological effects of pre-existing anti-PEG ant
papers.summary: This paper argues that inconsistent methods for detecting pre-existing anti-PEG antibodies have led to contradictory prevalence estimates and unclear understanding of their binding properties and clinical impact. The authors call for standardized detection approaches to clarify how these antibodies affect the efficacy and safety of PEGylated drugs.

papers.title: Heat-time-controlled chickpea protein aggregates: structure-function-digestibility interplay and Pickering emulsion performance.
papers.abstract: This study systematically investigated the modulation effects of heating duration (0-60 min) on the structure, functional properties, and Pickering emulsion performance of chickpea protein aggregates (CPAs). CPAs heated for 30 min (CPAs-30) exhibited favorable properties: the smallest particle size (534.67 nm) and zeta potential (-26.6 mV), and enhanced colloidal stability compared to other heating durations. Further mechanistic analysis revealed that a synergistic stabilization mechanism involving enhanced hydrophobic interactions (contact angle increased from 71.75° to 77.8°, surface hydroph
papers.summary: This study shows that heating duration controls the structure and function of chickpea protein aggregates, with 30 minutes of heating producing the smallest particles and best colloidal stability. These optimized aggregates form Pickering emulsions with improved performance through a synergistic stabilization mechanism involving enhanced hydrophobic interactions.

papers.title: Pharmacological insights into the antidiabetic potential of Rosa hybrida Hort. flowers based on enzyme inhibition and computational analysis.
papers.abstract: Rosa hybrida Hort. flowers are widely recognized for their ornamental value; however, their pharmacological potential, particularly as natural antidiabetic agents, remains insufficiently explored. This study aimed to evaluate the antioxidant and antidiabetic potential of Rosa hybrida Hort. flower extract using integrated in vitro and in silico approaches. The flower extract was prepared by ethanolic maceration following botanical authentication. Antioxidant activity was assessed using the DPPH radical scavenging assay, while total phenolic content (TPC) and total flavonoid content (TFC) were d
papers.summary: This study evaluates the antioxidant and antidiabetic potential of Rosa hybrida flower extract using both in vitro enzyme inhibition assays and computational (in silico) analyses. The extract showed measurable antioxidant activity and phenolic/flavonoid content, with computational docking suggesting interactions with diabetes-related enzyme targets. The work positions rose flower extracts as a potential natural source of antidiabetic compounds, though findings remain preliminary.

papers.title: HDX-MS-Guided computational modeling for rapid and accurate antibody-antigen interface mapping.
papers.abstract: Accurate mapping of paratopes and epitopes at antibody-antigen (Ab-Ag) interfaces is essential for the rational design of therapeutic antibodies in early drug development. Traditional methods for determining high-resolution Ab-Ag complex structures, such as X-ray crystallography and cryo-electron microscopy, are labor-intensive and require substantial time and resources. Although recent computational approaches have increased throughput, prediction accuracy and reliability remain limited, particularly without experimental structural constraints. Here, we present a hydrogen-deuterium exchange m
papers.summary: This paper presents a computational workflow that uses hydrogen-deuterium exchange mass spectrometry (HDX-MS) data as experimental constraints to guide antibody-antigen interface modeling. The approach aims to rapidly and accurately map paratopes and epitopes, addressing the bottleneck of traditional structural methods like X-ray crystallography and cryo-EM. It offers a practical tool for therapeutic antibody design by combining experimental and computational methods.

papers.title: Cryo-EM structure-based discovery of etravirine as a specific inhibitor of PRMT5/pICln protein-protein interaction for prostate cancer treatment.
papers.abstract: Protein arginine methyltransferase 5 (PRMT5) is overexpressed in many cancers and correlates with poor patient survival. In prostate cancer, PRMT5 cooperates with its cofactor pICln to promote tumour growth by epigenetically activating androgen receptor (AR) expression. Using a near-atomic cryo-EM structure of PRMT5/MEP50/pICln complex, we identified a previously undefined, pICln-specific protein-protein interaction (PPI) interface on PRMT5, termed P4I. Structure-based virtual screening identified the FDA-approved compound etravirine as a binder to this site. BiFC, Co-IP, and PLA assays confir
papers.journal: Journal of enzyme inhibition and medicinal chemistry
papers.summary: Using a near-atomic cryo-EM structure of the PRMT5/MEP50/pICln complex, the authors identified a previously undefined pICln-specific protein-protein interaction interface on PRMT5, termed P4I. Structure-based virtual screening of this site identified the FDA-approved drug etravirine as a specific inhibitor of the PRMT5/pICln interaction, with potential for prostate cancer treatment.

papers.title: Effects of Particle Size and Oxide Shell Thickness on the Oxidation Characteristics of Core-Shell Aluminum Nanoparticles Using Molecular Dynamics Simulation.
papers.abstract: Aluminum nanoparticles (ANPs) possess a core-shell structure, yet the coupled roles of atomic stress and interfacial charge transfer in their slow-heating oxidation remain elusive. This study employs ReaxFF molecular dynamics simulations to investigate the oxidation of six core-shell ANPs with different particle sizes (5-10 nm) and shell thicknesses (0.5-2.0 nm) from 300 K to 1400 K. Results reveal that the stress evolution dictates the oxidation pathway. Thin shells (0.5-1.0 nm) undergo a compressive-to-tensile stress transition, leading to shell rupture at ~1060 K and subsequent outflow and
papers.summary: This study uses ReaxFF molecular dynamics simulations to examine how particle size (5-10 nm) and oxide shell thickness (0.5-2.0 nm) affect the slow-heating oxidation of core-shell aluminum nanoparticles. The authors find that atomic stress evolution controls the oxidation pathway, with thin shells (0.5-1.0 nm) transitioning from compressive to tensile stress and rupturing at ~1060 K, allowing molten aluminum to flow outward.

papers.title: Antiviral Potential of Green-Synthesized Zinc Oxide and Copper Oxide Nanoparticles: Integrated In Vitro and In Silico Study.
papers.abstract: Viral infections such as human papillomavirus, rotavirus, and cytomegalovirus continue to pose significant global health challenges, causing persistent and widespread disease. The objective of this study is to evaluate the preliminary in vitro antiviral and cytotoxicity profile of zinc oxide (ZnO) and copper oxide (CuO) nanoparticles, which were synthesized through a green approach using Moringa oleifera leaf extract, against these viruses. Regarding antiviral effects, ZnO nanoparticles demonstrated potent antiviral activity against HPV, CMV, and rotavirus, with high selectivity indices and lo
papers.summary: This study synthesized zinc oxide and copper oxide nanoparticles using Moringa oleifera leaf extract and tested their antiviral activity against HPV, rotavirus, and cytomegalovirus in vitro, complemented by in silico docking analyses. ZnO nanoparticles showed potent antiviral effects with high selectivity indices, suggesting green-synthesized nanoparticles as promising antiviral candidates.

papers.title: Explainable AI reveals the allosteric blind spot in protein-ligand binding predictions.
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) has transformed prediction of protein structure and interactions, yet modeling of allosteric binding remains a persistent challenge. We develop an explainable AI framework that interrogates AI models AlphaFold3, Protenix, Boltz-2, Chai-1, and DynamicBind on rigorously stratified datasets of orthosteric and allosteric ligand-protein complexes. While AI models excel in accurate modeling of orthosteric ligand binding, a consistent and substantial performance gap observed across diverse architectures emerges in prediction of allosteric complexes. The biophysical logic
papers.summary: This study uses explainable AI to systematically test whether leading protein-ligand prediction models (AlphaFold3, Protenix, Boltz-2, Chai-1, DynamicBind) can handle allosteric binding sites. Across all architectures, the models perform well on orthosteric (primary) binding but show a consistent, substantial performance gap for allosteric complexes, revealing a shared blind spot in current AI methods.

papers.title: Multimodal molecular features enable interpretable umami peptide screening and structure-activity analysis.
papers.abstract: Umami peptides are important taste-active components in protein-rich foods, but their computational discovery is still constrained by predictors that rely mainly on sequence information and provide limited mechanistic interpretability. In this study, BioPP-GFD was developed as an interpretable multimodal deep learning framework for umami peptide screening and structure-activity analysis. The model integrates molecular graphs, molecular fingerprints, and physicochemical descriptors through adaptive channel attention. In the umami-bitter peptide classification task, BioPP-GFD achieved an accurac
papers.summary: This study presents BioPP-GFD, an interpretable multimodal deep learning framework that integrates molecular graphs, fingerprints, and physicochemical descriptors via adaptive channel attention to screen for umami peptides and analyze their structure-activity relationships. The model outperforms sequence-only predictors in distinguishing umami from bitter peptides while providing mechanistic interpretability.

papers.title: Identification of COPZ1 as a Shared Candidate Ferroptosis-Related Hub Gene in Periodontitis and Inflammatory Bowel Disease.
papers.abstract: Clinical and epidemiological evidence demonstrates a robust bidirectional link between inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) and periodontitis, with IBD patients having a significantly elevated risk of periodontitis. Although this association is well established, the shared molecular mechanisms remain unclear. Both IBD, including Crohn's disease (CD) and ulcerative colitis (UC), and periodontitis feature aberrant ferroptosis activation, which drives oxidative damage and tissue breakdown. We therefore hypothesized that ferroptosis is a core pathogenic mechanism common to all three conditions. Using
papers.summary: This study investigates the shared molecular mechanisms linking inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) and periodontitis, hypothesizing that ferroptosis—an iron-dependent form of cell death—is a common driver. Through bioinformatic analysis of gene expression datasets, the authors identify COPZ1 as a shared ferroptosis-related hub gene across Crohn's disease, ulcerative colitis, and periodontitis, suggesting it as a potential therapeutic target or biomarker.

papers.title: Novel Pyrazoline Derivatives as Therapeutic Candidate for Alzheimer's Disease: An Integrated Network Pharmacology and 3D-QSAR Modelling.
papers.abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is a complex neurodegenerative condition marked by amyloid-β accumulation, tau pathology, and neuroinflammation, while current single-target therapies largely provide symptomatic relief without effectively halting disease progression. Therefore, the rational design and synthesis of novel small molecules capable of simultaneously modulating multiple AD-related targets represent a promising therapeutic strategy. Based on this rationale, novel pyrazoline derivatives were synthesized and their therapeutic potential was evaluated using an integrative computational framework
papers.summary: This study synthesizes novel pyrazoline derivatives and evaluates their potential as multi-target therapeutics for Alzheimer's disease using network pharmacology and 3D-QSAR modeling. The integrated computational approach identifies compounds that may simultaneously modulate multiple AD-related targets, including amyloid-β, tau, and neuroinflammation pathways.

papers.title: Molecular and metabolic mechanisms of quercetin in liver fibrosis: an integrated network pharmacology, metabolomics, and molecular dynamics study.
papers.abstract: Liver fibrosis, a severe chronic liver injury sequela, lacks effective therapies. Quercetin, a natural flavonoid, exhibits multi-target anti-fibrotic potential.
papers.summary: This study integrates network pharmacology, metabolomics, and molecular dynamics simulations to uncover how quercetin, a natural flavonoid, combats liver fibrosis through multiple molecular and metabolic pathways. The multi-omics approach identifies key targets and metabolic perturbations, providing mechanistic insight into quercetin's anti-fibrotic effects. The findings support further development of quercetin as a therapeutic candidate for chronic liver injury.

papers.title: Endodontic potential of eugenol against Enterococcus faecalis: Antibacterial, antibiofilm, and network pharmacology insights.
papers.abstract: The present study aimed to evaluate the antibacterial and antibiofilm efficacy of eugenol against clinical isolates of Enterococcus faecalis obtained from persistent root canal infections and to investigate its potential interactions with virulence-associated target proteins using network pharmacology and molecular docking approaches.
papers.journal: Journal of oral biology and craniofacial research
papers.summary: This study evaluates eugenol, a natural compound, for its ability to kill and prevent biofilm formation by Enterococcus faecalis bacteria isolated from persistent root canal infections. It also uses network pharmacology and molecular docking to predict how eugenol interacts with bacterial proteins linked to virulence.

papers.title: Thymol and Limonene as Potent Antimicrobials: Bridging In Vitro Efficacy and Molecular Docking Insights.
papers.abstract: Nowadays, antimicrobial resistance has created an urgent need for elaborating effective and novel antibiotic agents. In effect, bioactive compounds derived from plants have attracted great interest due to their biological activities. This work intended to study and compare the antimicrobial effect of thymol and limonene against multiple clinical microorganisms including gram-positive bacteria, gram-negative bacteria, yeasts, and mycobacteria. Molecular docking and bioavailability prediction of thymol and limonene were also performed. The in vitro study was realized via disk diffusion technique
papers.summary: This study compares the antimicrobial activity of two plant-derived compounds, thymol and limonene, against a range of clinical pathogens including gram-positive and gram-negative bacteria, yeasts, and mycobacteria. The authors combine in vitro disk diffusion assays with molecular docking and bioavailability predictions to explore how these compounds might work at the molecular level. The work aims to bridge experimental efficacy data with computational insights to support the development of plant-based antimicrobial alternatives.

papers.title: Antiplasmodial Activity of Methylangolensate From Entandrophragma angolense (Welw.) C.DC. Stem Bark: An In Vitro and In Silico Approach.
papers.abstract: Previous investigation of the antiplasmodial effects of methylangolensate (MAL) has revealed promising activity against multiple strains of Plasmodium falciparum parasites. However, a significant gap still remains to be bridged regarding its potential as a lead compound for the development of novel drugs for the treatment of malaria. The study seeks to evaluate the multistage antiplasmodial effects, drug likeness, in silico ADMET properties, and possible drug targets of MAL against the P. falciparum parasites.
papers.summary: This study evaluates methylangolensate, a compound isolated from Entandrophragma angolense stem bark, for its anti-malarial potential against Plasmodium falciparum using both laboratory (in vitro) and computational (in silico) approaches. The authors assess its activity across multiple parasite life stages, predict drug-likeness and ADMET properties, and identify possible molecular targets. The findings aim to establish methylangolensate as a promising lead compound for new malaria drug development.

papers.title: Catechins as antibiofilm agents: molecular insights for virtual screening and in vitro biological evaluation.
papers.abstract: Bacterial Biofilms are of great concern because they are the main drivers of antimicrobial resistance. We investigated the potential of catechins against bacterial biofilms using advanced computational and in vitro models.
papers.summary: This study investigates catechins as potential antibiofilm agents against bacterial biofilms, which are key contributors to antimicrobial resistance. The authors combine computational virtual screening with in vitro biological assays to identify and evaluate catechin compounds for biofilm inhibition. The work provides molecular insights that could guide the development of new antibiofilm therapeutics.

papers.title: D-galactose enhances Maillard reaction and antioxidant activity of arginine-derived products: experimental and molecular insights.
papers.abstract: Arginine-derived Maillard reaction products (MRPs) have shown promising antioxidant activities. However, how structurally distinct hexose reducing sugars, such as D-fructose and D-galactose, affect the formation and functional properties of L-arginine-derived MRPs remains unclear.
papers.summary: This study compares how two different hexose sugars, D-fructose and D-galactose, affect the formation and antioxidant properties of Maillard reaction products derived from L-arginine. The authors find that D-galactose promotes the Maillard reaction more effectively and yields arginine-derived products with stronger antioxidant activity, supported by both experimental and molecular modeling insights.

papers.title: Association between TBPH exposure, increased MMP9 expression, and atherosclerosis: evidence from integrated network analysis and in vivo experiments.
papers.abstract: Bis(2-ethylhexyl)-2,3,4,5-tetrabromophthalate (TBPH) is used as a nonreactive brominated flame retardant used in industrial products, particularly in flexible polyvinyl chloride and rigid and flexible polyurethane foams. Although TBPH exposure poses potential health risks, its association with atherosclerosis remains poorly understood.
papers.summary: This study investigates whether exposure to the flame retardant TBPH is linked to atherosclerosis, using integrated network analysis combined with in vivo experiments. The authors report an association between TBPH exposure, increased expression of the matrix metalloproteinase MMP9, and atherosclerotic disease, suggesting a potential mechanistic pathway.

papers.title: A bioinformatic single-cell and structure-informed framework identifies a baicalin-CA2-keratinocyte state axis in atopic dermatitis.
papers.abstract: Atopic dermatitis (AD) is characterized by a self-reinforcing loop between epidermal barrier dysfunction and type 2-skewed inflammation; yet the most perturbed keratinocyte states and actionable epidermal targets remain incompletely defined. We integrated pharmacogenomic target mining, complementary machine-learning feature selection (LASSO and SVM-RFE), single-cell state-resolved perturbation analyses (Augur and scDist), and structure-based molecular modeling (molecular docking, MD simulation, and MM-PBSA free energy calculation) to prioritize candidate targets of baicalin in AD. CA2 emerged
papers.summary: This study integrates pharmacogenomic target mining, machine-learning feature selection, single-cell perturbation analyses, and structure-based modeling to identify CA2 as a key target of baicalin in atopic dermatitis. The authors propose a baicalin-CA2-keratinocyte state axis that links the compound to specific perturbed keratinocyte states, offering a framework for target prioritization in inflammatory skin disease.

papers.title: DBP-CanPred: a machine learning model for predicting cancer-causing mutations in DNA-binding proteins.
papers.abstract: The fundamental cellular processes, including transcriptional regulation, chromatin organization, and genome maintenance, are regulated by DNA-binding proteins (DBPs). Mutations in DBPs can alter protein-DNA interactions, leading to tumor development. However, identifying such driver mutations remains a major challenge due to limitations of experimental approaches.
papers.summary: DBP-CanPred is a machine learning model designed to predict cancer-causing mutations specifically in DNA-binding proteins. It addresses the challenge of identifying driver mutations that disrupt protein-DNA interactions, which are difficult to detect experimentally. The tool aims to aid in prioritizing potentially oncogenic mutations in this important protein class.

papers.title: Multi-state Structure Prediction of G Protein-Coupled Receptor Proteins via Prompting on AlphaFold.
papers.abstract: G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs), an essential family of transmembrane proteins, widely participate in signal transduction in organisms and have long been recognized as a major class of therapeutic targets. In structure-based drug design, high-resolution structures of GPCRs in both active and inactive states are essential for designing agonists and antagonists, respectively. However, obtaining experimental GPCR structures is costly, while homology modeling and artificial-intelligence-driven approaches including AlphaFold 2 and AlphaFold 3 often show reduced accuracy for active-state conform
papers.summary: This paper presents a method that uses prompt-based adaptation of AlphaFold to predict multiple conformational states (active and inactive) of G protein-coupled receptors, which are important drug targets. The approach addresses the reduced accuracy of standard AlphaFold predictions for active-state GPCR conformations, potentially aiding structure-based drug design of agonists and antagonists.

papers.title: A voyage of reprogrammable metabolic bioengineering reshapes plant defense: from editing tools to synthetic systems.
papers.abstract: Metabolic bioengineering has emerged as a transformative approach for reshaping plant defense by targeting intrinsic biosynthetic pathways to enhance immunity in modern agriculture. Moving beyond proof-of-concept metabolomics to broad-spectrum programmable pathway engineering addresses gaps in plant rational design and optimizes resilience in response to diverse environmental cues. This review aims to comprehensively highlight the transition of innovative approaches to phenolics, alkaloids, flavonoids, terpenoids, and benzoxazinoids, inferring adaptive reprogramming that mediates the growth-de
papers.summary: This review surveys how metabolic bioengineering can be used to reprogram plant biosynthetic pathways—such as those producing phenolics, alkaloids, flavonoids, terpenoids, and benzoxazinoids—to strengthen plant immunity. It traces the field's shift from proof-of-concept metabolomics toward programmable, broad-spectrum pathway engineering aimed at improving crop resilience in agriculture.

papers.title: PLK1/FOXM1-associated tumor-cell state and macrophage-related immune features in endometrial cancer.
papers.abstract: Polo-like kinase 1 (PLK1) and forkhead box M1 (FOXM1) have been widely studied in various cancers; however, their expression characteristics in endometrial cancer (EC) and their potential association with tumor microenvironment remodeling remain insufficiently characterized.
papers.summary: This study characterizes the expression of PLK1 and FOXM1 in endometrial cancer and links them to a specific tumor-cell state and macrophage-related immune features in the tumor microenvironment. The findings suggest that PLK1/FOXM1 activity may shape immune infiltration patterns in endometrial cancer.

papers.title: Naringenin as a dual-target modulator of RAGE-NF-κB signaling and Aβ fibrillization in Alzheimer's disease: integrated computational and experimental analyses.
papers.abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is a complex neurodegenerative disorder characterized by the accumulation and aggregation of β-amyloid (Aβ) and chronic neuroinflammation mediated by the receptor for advanced glycation end products (RAGE). Current therapeutic candidates targeting RAGE signaling or Aβ aggregation continue to face challenges, including off-target toxicity, poor blood-brain barrier (BBB) penetration, and limited multi-target efficacy.
papers.summary: This study investigates naringenin, a natural flavonoid, as a potential dual-target therapy for Alzheimer's disease. Using computational modeling and experimental assays, the authors show that naringenin can both inhibit RAGE-NF-κB inflammatory signaling and interfere with Aβ fibrillization, suggesting it may address two key pathological mechanisms simultaneously.

papers.title: Nanogel-Based Precision Bone Regeneration: Rational Design, Biological Barrier Penetration, and Osteoporotic Microenvironment Remodeling.
papers.abstract: The pathogenesis of osteoporosis is primarily associated with impaired communication between osteoblasts and osteoclasts, leading to disrupted bone homeostasis. Conventional biomaterials mainly rely on macroscopic structural support and are limited in their ability to precisely regulate the complex bone microenvironment and overcome biological barriers. As representative soft matter nanoplatforms, nanogels possess unique viscoelastic mechanical properties and adaptive biointerfacial properties, offering new opportunities to overcome physical barriers within bone tissues. Moving beyond previous
papers.summary: This review discusses how nanogel-based platforms can be rationally designed to treat osteoporosis by penetrating biological barriers in bone tissue and remodeling the impaired communication between osteoblasts and osteoclasts. It highlights the viscoelastic and adaptive biointerfacial properties of nanogels that enable precise regulation of the bone microenvironment beyond conventional macroscopic biomaterials.
